doc.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

title: The 'thee' pronunciation riff
summary: A humorous digression on pronouncing 'the' as 'thee' before vowels, which he may turn into a song.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: “Thee” article, or the article. The article is hard to say. The article. But thee article just, just thee article. The ball is the ball. And you find that in the English language when you want something that flows nicely, the should be pronounced “thee” in front of vowels, and the in front of consonants. And I’m just walking through, now I’ll probably have to write a song about that. Because that was never in an English book was it? Did you ever read that in an English book?

But in terms of pronunciation it always makes sense, that it should be the lamp, the book, thee aardvark. See but aardvark is hard to say but the aardvark is just thee aardvark. Thee, because of the a.
Thee ideas you have are quite fascinating.
Right thank you. See you caught on immediately, even better than I’d hoped.
I’m going to try that in my next song. Actually it does flow nice, and I expect if I see your show on Broadway I expect the singers will be using that. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -12-
I will probably be the only singer. But I think I have to write a song about that, because it’s a very good idea. To let America learn how to speak our language.
